title: Lamar Middle School Names Its Football Field for Roque Vela Sr., Veteran and Former LISD Board President
excerpt: M.B. Lamar Middle School dedicated its football field to Roque Vela Sr. on Nov. 13, honoring the Vietnam veteran, former LISD board president and Webb County commissioner.
content:
M.B. Lamar Middle School in Laredo named its football field for Roque Vela Sr. during a dedication ceremony on Thursday, Nov. 13, honoring a Vietnam veteran whose decades of service touched the school district, the county, and the city's veterans community, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Vela entered the U.S. Army at 17 and served in Vietnam, earning the Purple Heart and the Army Commendation Medal with device for valor. After returning to Laredo, he built a business career and served 12 years on the Laredo Independent School District Board of Trustees, including time as board president, and four years as a Webb County commissioner. He also chaired the City of Laredo Veterans Affairs Committee until his death, and his family attended the school, the Times reported.

Vela's family, LISD officials and trustees, students and community members attended the ceremony. The J.W. Nixon High School Junior ROTC Color Guard presented the colors, and the Lamar Middle School orchestra performed the national anthem. District officials and Vela's family spoke at the event.

His son, former Councilmember Roque Vela Jr., said: “To know that my father's name is going to live on, and particularly on this football field at this school, is a huge honor.” He said his family was totally honored and thanked the board of trustees, and he said he hopes future students will see the name and ask who his father was.

His daughter Yvonne Vela Leal reflected on her father's path from humble beginnings through military service, business ownership and community leadership, saying his greatest gift was the example he set through his work ethic, determination and belief in education.

LISD Board of Trustees Secretary Dr. Gilberto “Gil” Martinez Jr., who said he helped nominate Vela for the honor, recalled that Vela checked on him after he broke his foot in high school to make sure he kept up with his schoolwork.

Vela's name is also expected to be added to a soccer complex near the family business, Jett Bowl North. The Laredo City Council approved renaming a section of the Bartlett Soccer Complex in his honor in August, and an official date for that ceremony was still pending at publication, the Times reported.
